(p-87) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
Surah Al-'Asr (The Declining Day)

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿By time,﴾ ﴿indeed, mankind is in loss.﴾

Al-'Asr is a name for the whole of time or a part of it.

For this reason, the intended meaning of it has been disputed, since it is not clarified here.

It has been said: it is the entire dahr (lifetime of the world), by which Allah swore because of what it contains of wonders: a nation passes and another nation comes, a decree is executed, and a sign appears. It is itself unchanging: a night followed by a day, and a day chased by a night. Thus it is in itself a marvel, as has been said:

Existent, resembling the non-existent, and moving, resembling the still.

As has been said:

"I see time as a ship sailing with us toward death, and we do not see its movements."

Thus it is in itself a sign, whether in its past, where one does not know when it began; or in its present, where one does not know how it passes; or in its future.

This view is supported by what has been transmitted as a mawquf (halted) report from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, and as a marfu' (raised) report from an irregular recitation: "By time, and the calamities of the dahr." It is taken as an explanation, if it is not authentic as Qur'an. This meaning is also reported from Ibn 'Abbas.

On this is the poet's saying:

"The path of desire is rough, and the sea of desire is deep; the day of desire is a month, and the month of desire is a dahr."

It has also been said that al-'Asr is the night and the day.

(p-88) Humayd ibn Thawr said:

"The two 'asrs did not tarry, a day and a night, when they sought to reach what they would complete."

Al-'Asran also means the morning (al-ghadah) and the evening (al-'ashiy).

As has been said:

"I delay him with the two 'asrs until he tires of me, and he accepts half the debt, while his nose is humbled."

Al-matl means procrastination and delaying a debt.

As has been said:

"Every debtor has paid and fulfilled his creditor, while the one who delays, whose creditor is wearied, is oppressed."

It has also been said that al-'ashiy is what comes after the sun's decline until its setting. This is the view of al-Hasan and Qatadah.

From this is the poet's saying:

"Let us go out, O 'Amr, the 'asr has grown short, and in the first going-out is the spoil and the reward."

It is also reported from Qatadah: it is the last hour of the hours of the day, to magnify the oath by it, and because Allah swears by the dawn and the forenoon.

It has been said: it is the prayer of 'Asr, because it is the middle (prayer).

It has been said: it is the era of the Prophet ﷺ or the time of his nation, because it resembles the afternoon of the life of the world.

What appears to be the case, and Allah knows best, is that the closest of all these views are two: either generality in the sense of dahr, due to the irregular recitation, since its lowest level is that of explanation, and because its generality encompasses the rest of the views;

or the "'asr" of the human being, that is, his lifespan and the duration of his life, which is the place of gain and loss, as indicated by the context, and because it particularly concerns the servant himself as an admonition and benefit.

This second meaning is strengthened by what surrounds this surah: the preceding Surah al-Takathur and the following Surah al-Humazah. The former censures this distraction and competition in wealth and children, even visiting graves at death, and the place of all this is the life of the human being.

(p-89) Surah al-Humazah, in essence and approximately the same meaning, says: ﴿who gathers wealth and counts it﴾, ﴿he thinks his wealth will make him immortal.﴾ [al-Humazah: 2-3]

So gathering wealth and counting it occurs in the life of the human being, and his life is limited, not made eternal in this world; just as faith and righteous deeds are linked to the life of the human being.

Accordingly, the meaning of al-'Asr in this surah is either generality, since it includes all, and due to the irregular recitation, and this is the strongest;

or the life of the human being, because it is most binding on him in his work, and all other usages are from the usage of the whole for a part.

And Allah knows best.

His saying: ﴿indeed, mankind is in loss.﴾

The word al-insan, though singular, has the article al- which makes it generic.

Shaykh (may Allah's mercy be upon him and upon us) clarified this in order to remove the appearance of inconsistency, and the notice of it has been given many times before. It therefore includes both the Muslim and the disbeliever, except those whom Allah excepts.

It has been said: it is specific to the disbeliever, but the first is stronger for its generality.

And ﴿indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ is the answer to the oath. Al-khusr (loss) has been said to mean a bad bargain (ghabn), a deficiency (naqs), a punishment ('uqubah), or destruction (halakah). All are close in meaning.

The root of khusr and khusran is like kufr and kufran: a deficiency in the capital. Here it does not specify the type of loss or in what it occurs, but is stated in general so as to encompass all. The particle of place (fi) is used to indicate that the human being is immersed in loss and surrounded by it from every direction.

If we consider two things, namely the exception and the surah before it, this generality becomes clear, because the implied meaning of the exception includes four matters: lack of faith, which is disbelief; lack of righteous deeds, which is corrupt action; lack of mutual exhortation to truth, which is either complete absence of mutual exhortation or exhortation to falsehood; and lack of mutual exhortation to patience, which is either complete absence of it or anxiety and impatience.

The preceding surah describes the human being's distraction by competition in wealth and children, seeking riches and increase therein; its opposite is the loss of wealth and children, which is khusran.

(p-90) Accordingly, loss in religion occurs in terms of faith through disbelief, and in Islam through abandoning action, although faith in the technical sense includes this; and in distraction in falsehood and abandoning truth; and in anxiety and fear.

Hence also the abandonment of commanding good and forbidding evil in what benefits the servant's success, the soundness of his religion and his worldly life. All of this is indicated in the Qur'an, which we summarize as follows:

As for loss through disbelief, as in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿If you associate others with Allah, your deeds will surely be lost, and you will surely be among the losers.﴾ [al-Zumar: 65]

And His saying: ﴿Those who denied the meeting with Allah have certainly lost,﴾ meaning: because they did not work for this meeting, and they fell short in their affair in the life of this world, so they wasted themselves and their share in the Hereafter.

As for loss through abandoning action, as in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And whoever's scales are light, those are they who have lost themselves﴾ [al-A'raf: 9], because the scales are the measures of deeds, as mentioned earlier: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 7].

Similar to this: ﴿And whoever takes Satan as a protector instead of Allah has certainly suffered a clear loss﴾ [al-Nisa': 119], because he will be of the party of Satan: ﴿Unquestionably, the party of Satan are the losers﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 19], meaning by obeying him in disobedience to Allah.

As for loss through abandoning mutual exhortation to truth, there is nothing after truth but error, and truth is Islam in its entirety. Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him, and he will be among the losers in the Hereafter﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 85].

As for loss through abandoning mutual exhortation to patience and falling into anxiety and fear, as Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And among the people is he who worships Allah on an edge; if good touches him, he is content with it, but if a trial befalls him, he turns back on his face. He has lost this world and the Hereafter. That is the clear loss﴾ [al-Hajj: 11].

* * *

Verifying the Reality of Human Loss

They agreed that the capital of a human being in his life is his lifespan; he is charged with spending it during his existence in this world, which is for him like a marketplace. If he spends it in good, he profits; if he spends it in evil, he loses.

(p-91) This meaning is indicated by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their souls and their wealth in exchange for Paradise﴾ [al-Tawbah: 111], to the end of the verse.

And His saying: ﴿Shall I direct you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment? You believe in Allah and His Messenger﴾ [al-Saff: 10-11], to the end of the verse.

In the Hadith in Muslim: "Purity is half of faith." And at its end: "Every person goes forth in the morning, selling his soul, and either freeing it or destroying it," which emphasizes that the capital of a human being is his lifespan.

Because of the importance of this lifespan, it is paired with the mission and the warning in His saying: ﴿Did We not give you a lifespan in which whoever would remember could remember, and the warner came to you?﴾ [Fatir: 37].

On this basis they said: Allah, may He be exalted, sent His Messenger with guidance, and guided every human being to the two paths, and placed for every human being a station in Paradise and a station in Hellfire.

Whoever believes and does righteous deeds, his destination is the station of Paradise, and he is spared the station of Hellfire. Whoever disbelieves, his destination is the station of Hellfire, and he forfeits his station in Paradise.

As indicated in the Hadith of the grave: "When he first enters his grave, if he is a believer, a door to Hellfire is opened for him, and it is said to him: 'That is your seat in the Fire, had you not believed.' Then it is closed, and a door to Paradise is opened for him, and it is said to him: 'This is your abode, until the Hour rises.' He says: 'My Lord, establish the Hour!'"

If he is a disbeliever, it is entirely the reverse. When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of Hellfire enter Hellfire, each takes his station in it. The stations of the people of Hellfire in Paradise remain empty and are inherited by the people of Paradise, and the stations of the people of Paradise in Hellfire remain empty and are distributed among the people of Hellfire. Here the manifest loss appears: whoever forfeits a station in Paradise and goes to a station in Hellfire is undoubtedly a loser, and whoever forfeits his station in Paradise for another and takes in its place the station of another in Hellfire, that is the manifest loss, we seek refuge in Allah.

As for the non-disbeliever and the general body of Muslims, the loss lies in negligence, such that if he enters Paradise but does not attain the highest ranks, he feels the loss at the time in which he neglected, and did not compete in doing good to attain the highest ranks.

So this surah in fact drives every individual to diligence and profitable work, and the ranks of Paradise are lofty, and its stations are high, however much the servant exerts himself; for ahead of him is room for gain and profit. We ask Allah for success and prosperity.

It has been said: no person leaves this world except in sorrow. If he was a wrongdoer, it is over his wrongdoing; if he was a doer of good, it is over his shortcoming. This meaning may be witnessed by His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast, the angels will descend upon them, saying, "Do not fear and do not grieve, but rejoice in Paradise which you were promised."﴾ [Fussilat: 30]

So fear is of the future before them, and grief is over the past behind them. And Allah knows best.

What demonstrates the gravity of this matter is that when a human being reaches the end of his life, and feels his limited days and bounded hours, and wishes for an added day in which to provision himself, or a brief hour in which to make up for some of what he missed, he finds no way to do so. Then he feels regret and sorrow over the days, nights, months, and years that were wasted on him without gain or benefit, which could have been profitable for him. In the authentic Hadith: "Two blessings in which many people are deceived: health and free time."

That is: they pass by without being used in the complete avenues of gain, so they are lost to him without any compensation worth mentioning, and then he regrets, but it is too late for regret.

As has been said about this:

"The forelock has been exchanged for a bald head, and for the bright pearl-like teeth, a pearl-less gap; just as the Muslim bought Christianity when he became a Christian."

* * *

A Note

In Surah al-Takathur there is a censure of distraction by competing in wealth, children, and the like, and then an indication that its cause is ignorance, for if they knew with certainty, that distraction would not have occupied them until death overtook them.

Here too there is an indication that the cause of this loss into which the human being falls is ignorance, which leads to disbelief and persistence in falsehood. This is supported by the hardness of the heart and long hope, as Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Has the time not come for those who believe that their hearts should humble themselves to the remembrance of Allah and what has descended of the truth, and that they should not be like those who were given the Scripture before, and the term grew long for them, so their hearts became hard? And many of them are defiantly disobedient.﴾ [al-Hadid: 16]

Another Note

﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ specifies mankind in what has preceded. But another verse indicates that jinn are like mankind, in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Those are they against whom the word has come into effect among nations that had passed on before them of jinn and mankind; indeed, they were losers.﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 18]

The explanation of the charge of jinn with the call, their response to it, and their calling others to it has already been given.

⁕ ⁕ ⁕

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

(p-465) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
Surah Al-'Asr

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿By time﴾ ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾.

This noble verse, its apparent meaning indicates that the one spoken of as being in loss is a single person, as evidenced by the singular form of the word "al-insan" (the human being) and the exception made from that single human being in the wording.

His saying: ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ [al-Asr: 3] requires that it is not a single person.

The answer to this is: although the word "al-insan" is singular, the definite article "al" (alif and lam) for comprehensiveness (al-istighraq) turns the singular noun, by means of these two, into a form of generality. Accordingly, the meaning of "inna al-insan" is that every human being is included, by virtue of the comprehensive "al" indicating this.

And knowledge is with Allah the Exalted.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 103, verse 3:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds, and exhort one another to the truth, and exhort one another to patience﴾.

This is the exception from the preceding "man" (humankind), which indicates generality, as we have previously mentioned. Faith (al-iman) linguistically means affirmation (al-tasdiq), and in the Sharia it means the firm conviction in the six pillars of faith, as in the hadith of Jibril, peace be upon him, with the Messenger ﷺ when he asked him about Islam, faith and excellence (ihsan).

"And do righteous deeds": the conjunction (al-'atf) requires difference (al-mughayara).

For this reason some people said that deeds are not included in the definition of faith, and their statements are well known.

The majority hold that faith is conviction in the heart, verbal utterance by the tongue, and action by the limbs.

So action is included in it, and it increases and decreases. We have previously mentioned that action is a condition closer to being a part, meaning that faith is realized by conviction and its existence does not depend on action; but action is a condition for benefiting from faith, when the servant is able to act. Among what indicates that faith is realized by the definition of conviction and utterance, even if the servant is not able to act, is the story of the Companion who embraced Islam at the start of the battle, fought, was martyred, and did not pray a single rak'ah to Allah, and entered Paradise.

The majority hold that mere conviction does not benefit its holder, as the uncle of the Prophet ﷺ believed in the truth of his message but did not utter a word by which he could argue for him ﷺ. Likewise, if one believes and utters the two testimonies but does not act, he contradicts his own statement.

We have previously discussed this issue in detail.

"Righteous deeds" (al-salihat) is the plural of salihah. The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on us and him, has previously defined it, and the conditions for a deed to be righteous, by their evidences: that it conforms to the Book of Allah, that its doer performs it sincerely for the sake of Allah, and that it proceeds from a believer in Allah, etc.

His saying: ﴿and exhort one another to the truth﴾.

Exhorting one another to the truth is considered the specific after the general, because it is included in doing righteous deeds.

It was said: exhorting one another means that some of them advise others to the truth.

It was said: the truth is everything that is the opposite of falsehood, so it includes performing acts of obedience and abandoning sins.

He considered this a foundation of the principles of enjoining good and forbidding evil, by the indication of the pairing with exhorting one another to patience, i.e., regarding enjoining and forbidding, as will come, Allah willing.

It was said: the truth is the Qur'an, because it encompasses every command, every prohibition, and all good. Evidence for this is His saying, may He be exalted, concerning the Qur'an: ﴿And with the truth We sent it down, and with the truth it descended﴾ [al-Isra': 105].

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, so worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion﴾ [al-Zumar: 2].

The verses of the Qur'an indicate that the exhortation to the truth includes the whole Sharia, its roots and its branches, what came before and what is present. Among that is what Allah enjoined upon the prophets, and in general, from Noah, Abraham and those after them, in His saying: ﴿He has ordained for you of the religion what He enjoined upon Noah, and that which We revealed to you, and what We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses and Jesus: that you establish the religion and do not be divided therein﴾ [ash-Shura: 13].

Establishing the religion means upholding it in its entirety. This enjoinment was the work of the messengers for their nations and those after them. Abraham, peace be upon him, carried it out, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And Abraham enjoined it upon his sons, and Jacob: "O my sons, indeed Allah has chosen for you the religion, so do not die except while you are Muslims"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 132].

And after Abraham, Jacob, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Or were you witnesses when death approached Jacob, when he said to his sons, "What will you worship after me?" They said, "We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham, Ishmael and Isaac, one God, and to Him we are Muslims"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 133].

(p-95) Thus is the exhortation of the nations to the root of faith and the generality of the Sharia, and likewise to worship, such as prayer and zakat, as in the saying of Allah concerning His prophet Jesus, peace be upon him: ﴿And He has enjoined upon me prayer and zakat as long as I am alive﴾ ﴿and dutiful to my mother﴾ [Maryam: 31-32].

Likewise, the social condition is evident in the enjoinment concerning parents and children, for the cohesion of the family. Regarding parents, Allah says: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man concerning his parents: his mother carried him in weakness upon weakness, and his weaning is in two years — "Be grateful to Me and to your parents; to Me is the destination." ﴾ ﴿But if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them, and accompany them in this world with kindness﴾ [Luqman: 14-15].

Regarding children, He said: ﴿Allah instructs you concerning your children: for the male, the equal of the share of two females﴾ [an-Nisa': 11].

Regarding general rights, there are commands and prohibitions, acts of worship and transactions. The verses of the Ten Injunctions came, concerning which Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Whoever wishes to look at the will of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ upon which is his seal, let him recite: ﴿Say, "Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited for you: that you associate nothing with Him, and be good to parents, and do not kill your children out of poverty — We provide for you and for them — and do not approach immoral deeds, what is apparent of them and what is concealed, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right. This He has instructed you that you may reason."﴾ ﴿And do not approach the property of the orphan except in the best manner until he reaches maturity. And give full measure and weight in justice. We do not charge a soul except [according to] its capacity. And when you speak, be just, even if it should be [against] a near relative. And to the covenant of Allah fulfill. This He has instructed you that you may remember.﴾ ﴿And indeed, this is My path, [being] straight, so follow it. And do not follow [other] ways, for they will separate you from His way. This He has instructed you that you may become righteous.﴾ [al-An'am: 151-153].

Those are the comprehensive injunctions that open the doors of good and close the doors of evil, and are concluded by this clarification and definition: ﴿And indeed, this is My path, [being] straight, so follow it. And do not follow the [other] ways﴾.

If we wished to connect this with the exhortation to the truth, and with it and with the Opening of the Book, the result would be as follows in His saying: ﴿and exhort one another to the truth﴾, referring to those injunctions, which are comprehensive and all-inclusive, and are titled as being the straight path of Allah.

(p-96) It is as if His saying: ﴿and exhort one another to the truth﴾ is equivalent to His saying: and exhort one another to the straight path, and be steadfast upon it.

Then in Surat al-Fatihah: ﴿Guide us to the straight path﴾ [al-Fatihah: 6], and this is the straight path of Allah, so follow it.

Thus Surat al-'Asr includes the exhortation to steadfastness upon the straight path of Allah and following it. And following it, His saying: ﴿and exhort one another to patience﴾ [al-'Asr: 3] comes as a reinforcement of this straight path, since patience is necessary for performing acts of obedience, just as it is necessary for abstaining from forbidden things.

These ten injunctions combined commanding and forbidding, doing and abstaining. Likewise, there is in them an indication of what the callers to Islam say: that righteous deeds, calling to the truth and exhorting one another to it, involve enjoining good and forbidding evil, and whoever undertakes this is generally exposed to the harm of people. Therefore, exhorting one another to patience became obligatory for them, just as Luqman said to his son, advising him, and combining in his advice the counsel of Surat al-'Asr when he said: ﴿O my son, establish prayer, enjoin what is good, forbid what is wrong, and bear patiently what befalls you. Indeed, that is of the matters requiring determination.﴾ [Luqman: 17].

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on us and him, has previously explained in detail the rules of enjoining good and forbidding evil at His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, upon you is yourselves; no one who has strayed can harm you if you are [rightly] guided﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 105], in Surat al-Ma'idah.

Thus this surah has truly become comprehensive of the principles of the message.

As has been narrated from al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, that he said: "If people were to reflect upon this surah, it would suffice them."

His saying: ﴿and exhort one another to the truth﴾. The encouragement to exhort one another to mercy also came alongside patience, in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then he was among those who believed and exhorted one another to patience and exhorted one another to compassion﴾ [al-Balad: 17].

With these three injunctions: exhorting one another to the truth, exhorting one another to patience, and exhorting one another to compassion, the components of the complete society are completed, whose foundation is the finest virtues and the most excellent values.

Because exhorting one another to the truth establishes the truth and steadfastness upon the straight way.

(p-97) And by exhorting one another to patience, they are able to continue their journey upon this path and overcome every obstacle that confronts them.

And by exhorting one another to compassion, they become bound together like one body. These are gifts that none but the Qur'an has given, and it has given them in this concise surah. And success is from Allah.

A NOTE

Al-Fakhr al-Razi said: When Allah, the Exalted, informed about these people of their salvation from loss, and their success through righteous deeds and faith, He informed about them that they did not suffice with what concerned themselves alone, but went beyond to others, calling them to what they had attained, in accordance with his, the Prophet's ﷺ, saying: "Love for your brother what you love for yourself." End of quotation, summarized.

Evidence for this is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast, the angels will descend upon them…﴾ up to His saying ﴿And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah, does righteous deeds, and says, "Indeed, I am of the Muslims"? And not equal are the good deed and the bad. Repel [evil] by that which is better, and thereupon the one between you and him enmity [will become] as if he were a devoted friend. But none is granted it except those who are patient, and none is granted it except one of great fortune﴾ [Fussilat: 30-35].

Allah has clarified that people are of three categories in the face of the call of the messengers.

A people who believed, said "Our Lord is Allah," and remained steadfast upon that through righteous deeds.

A people whose aspirations rose to calling others, and they are without doubt the best in speech.

And a people who opposed the callers and harmed them.

Then He clarified the position of the callers toward those evildoers within His saying: ﴿And not equal are the good deed and the bad. Repel…﴾, meaning: repel the evildoers' harm with that which is better, so they become your friends. He also clarified that this station ﴿none is granted it except those who are patient﴾, and then He clarified that whoever rises to it and takes its path, indeed he is one of great fortune.

A NOTE

I had heard from the Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on us and him, his saying that for the callers there are two enemies: one from mankind, and the other from the devils.

Allah has guided us to how to overcome both of them and to ward off their evil.

As for the enmity of mankind, it is met by repaying evil with good, whereupon he becomes a devoted friend.

As for the enemy from the jinn, it is by seeking refuge from him: ﴿And if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing﴾ [Fussilat: 36].

We ask Allah, the Exalted, for guidance and success.

We have indicated that the Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on us and him, presented the topic of enjoining good and forbidding evil at His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, upon you is yourselves; no one who has strayed can harm you if you are guided﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 105].

He mentioned Surat al-'Asr there, and established several issues concerning the method of enjoining good and forbidding evil, to a degree that is indispensable.
